I spent two years trying to run a faceless TikTok page. Turns out I was never supposed to be making the videos at all.

Every night after work, the same routine.

Come up with an idea. Write the script. Record the voiceover, delete it, record it again. Find the visuals. Line up the captions. Export. Upload. Pick a posting time. Post.

Two to three hours. For one video. Every single night.

I did it for eight months straight. The page got to 900 followers.

Then work got busy and I missed a day. Then three. The views dropped. The page flatlined. I quit.

With us you'll only open your page to watch it grow.

Own a growing page. Skip the grind.

Start today and go from picking a niche to posting daily in about five minutes.

My cousin fell asleep on his couch at 9:40 last Friday. His faceless page was still posting new videos.

I was at his place to watch the game. He passed out before halftime. Long work week, I get it.

Around 10 his phone lit up on the coffee table.

Then again. And again.

I leaned over. Notifications stacking up. TikTok. YouTube. Instagram.

"Your video was posted." "Your video is trending." "+180 new followers."

I woke him up and told him his phone was blowing up.

He looked at it for two seconds, said "oh nice, it posted," and closed his eyes again.

Posted? You were asleep. Who posted it?
